rektion: etw. in etw. (Akk.) eintauchen (hat); in etw. (Akk.) eintauchen (ist; auch fig.: in eine andere Welt / Kultur eintauchen)
meaning_en: to dip (sth. into sth.); to plunge/dive into; fig.: to immerse oneself in
definition_de: etwas kurz in eine Flüssigkeit tauchen; selbst in Wasser hineingehen; übertragen: sich ganz auf etwas einlassen (in eine fremde Kultur / in ein Buch eintauchen)
example_de: Mein Opa taucht jeden Morgen sein Croissant kurz in den großen Milchkaffee ein.
example_en: Every morning my grandpa briefly dips his croissant into his big milky coffee.
visual_idea: Collocation 'etw. in Kaffee eintauchen': a croissant half sunk into a big cup, its soaked darker end making ein- (into) visible, a cosy everyday ritual. Rejected: a diver plunging into a lake (the moment of impact is drawn badly, and the underwater boy is already 'untertauchen') and 'in eine andere Welt eintauchen' (a reader with a book reads as 'lesen'). The figurative use is in definition_de.
image_prompt: close-up of a breakfast table by a sunny window: an old man's hand holds a golden croissant whose lower half is sunk deep into a large white cup of milky coffee, the coffee rippling around it, the soaked part dark and wet, crumbs on a small plate, a jar of jam, the old man's smiling face softly blurred behind
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: close-up at a breakfast table: an old man's hand slowly dips a golden croissant into a large white cup of milky coffee, holds it there for a moment, then lifts it out with the soaked end dripping; static camera
